safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(ويل) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: the wording indicates a supplication, so it was valid to begin with an indefinite noun.], (لكلّ) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, (لمزة) is a naʿt of همزة, genitive like it [Note: it was said that it is a verbal tawkīd by synonymy, like their saying ʿifrīt nifrīt.]..
Clause: «ويل لكلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
2-3 (الذي) is a relative, a badal of (كلّ) [Note: it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", the clause then being an explanatory resumption.], in the position of genitive..
And the clause: «جمع ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «عدّده ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «يحسب ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the agent of عدّد [Note: or an explanatory resumption with no grammatical position.]..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ ماله أخلده..) is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of يحسب.
And the clause: «أخلده» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ.

* Morphology:
(1) همزة: an intensive form, i.e. one who does much hamz (slandering); the tāʾ in it is for intensification; its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma and two fatḥas [Note: the form فعلة – with ḍamma and fatḥa – is regularly built for intensification of the agent, and فعلة – with ḍamma and sukūn – for intensification of the patient.
One says: a man laʿana (with ḍamma then fatḥa) for one who curses others a great deal, and a man laʿna (with ḍamma then sukūn) for one whom people curse and curse often.].
(لمزة): like همزة in form and meaning.. In al-Mukhtār: al-hamz is like al-lamz in form and meaning, and its class is ضرب; and it also says: al-lamz is faulting, and its origin is signalling with the eye, and its class is ضرب and نصر.

* Benefits:
- What counts is the generality of the meaning, not the specificity of the occasion: The exegetes differed about whom this sūra was revealed concerning. It was said: it was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq ibn Wahb, who used to attack people and backbite them. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: We kept hearing that Sūrat al-Humaza was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī. It was said: it was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who used to backbite the Prophet ﷺ behind his back and revile him to his face. And it was said it was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī. And it was said: it is general, concerning every person with this description, whoever he may be, because the specificity of the occasion does not detract from the generality of the wording and the ruling.

safi-cedvel:4-9.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is for rebuke and reproach. (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (ينبذنّ) is a passive imperfect, indeclinable on fatḥa in the position of nominative, and (the nūn) is the nūn of emphasis; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. the slanderer, the backbiter. (في الحطمة) is attached to (ينبذنّ).
Clause: «ينبذنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
5-7 (the wāw) is parenthetical. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ, in both places. (نار) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي". (الموقدة) is a naʿt of نار. (التي) is a relative in the position of nominative, a second naʿt of نار. (على الأفئدة) is attached to (تطّلع)..
And the clause: «ما أدراك ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause: «أدراك ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «ما الحطمة» is in the position of accusative, the second direct object of the verb أدراك.
And the clause: « (هي) نار الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «تطّلع ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (التي).
8-9 (عليهم) is attached to (مؤصدة), (في عمد) is attached to an omitted element, a second khabar of (إنّ)..
And the clause: «إنّها ... مؤصدة» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(4) الحطمة: an intensive form, its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma and two fatḥas, from the triliteral حطم (class of ضرب) meaning "to break"; it is used in the noble verse as a name for the Fire because it shatters whatever it swallows.
(6) الموقدة: the feminine of الموقد, a passive participle from the quadriliteral أوقد; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(9) ممدّدة: the feminine of الممدّد, a passive participle from the quadriliteral مدّد; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Muqābala (antithesis/correspondence): in His saying, the Exalted: «لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ», after His saying, the Exalted: «وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ».
A verbal correspondence of remarkable eloquence: when He branded him with this mark, in a form indicating that it is firmly rooted and settled in him, He followed the repeated intensification in الهمزة and اللمزة with the threat of the Fire that He named الحطمة, because of the terror he suffers in it and the torment cast upon him there. In naming it He chose an intensive form on the pattern of the form that contained the sin committed, so that balance is achieved between the sin and the recompense.
